what_its_for: Oxandrolone is a medicine used to help patients gain weight after surgery, a long illness, or a serious injury. It is also used to treat bone pain caused by osteoporosis (weak bones) and to help patients who have lost too much weight due to certain medical conditions. It belongs to a group of medicines called anabolic steroids, which help the body build protein and muscle.
how_to_take: Take oxandrolone by mouth with or without food. If this medicine upsets your stomach, try taking it with food or milk. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush or chew the tablet unless your doctor tells you to. Follow your doctor's instructions carefully and do not take more or less than prescribed.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 2.5 mg to 20 mg per day, divided into 2 to 4 smaller doses throughout the day. Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your medical condition, weight, and how your body responds to the medicine. For children, the dose is based on body weight and will be determined by the doctor. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first. Most courses of treatment last 2 to 4 weeks, and your doctor may repeat the treatment after a short break if needed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist for advice.
storage: Store oxandrolone at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet. Ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of medicine you no longer need.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can increase the risk of liver problems. Do not take any new prescription medicines, over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, or herbal supplements without first checking with your doctor or pharmacist, as some medicines can interact with oxandrolone. Avoid activities that could increase your risk of injury, since this medicine can affect bone health. Women who are pregnant or planning to become pregnant should not take this medicine, as it can harm an unborn baby. This medicine is a controlled substance — do not share it with anyone else, as misuse can cause serious health problems.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you notice any of the following: yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes (signs of liver problems), dark-colored urine or pale-colored stools, severe stomach or abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting that does not go away, swelling of your ankles or feet, unusual weight gain, trouble breathing, chest pain, changes in your menstrual period (for women), signs of masculinization in women such as deepening voice, increased facial or body hair, or enlarged clitoris, increased or painful erections in men, signs of depression or mood changes, or any signs of allergic reaction such as rash, itching, or swelling of the face, lips, or throat.
when_it_works: Some patients may start to notice improvements in weight and strength within a few weeks of starting treatment. However, the full benefit of this medicine may take several weeks to months depending on your condition. Keep taking the medicine as prescribed even if you do not feel immediate results. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular check-ups and blood tests to make sure the medicine is working and is safe for you.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): Use with caution. Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects, especially liver problems and prostate issues in men. Regular monitoring by your doctor is important. Children and teenagers: This medicine can affect bone growth and development in young patients. Your doctor will carefully weigh the benefits and risks before prescribing it to children. Pregnant women: Do NOT use this medicine during pregnancy. It can cause serious harm or birth defects to an unborn baby. Use effective birth control while taking this medicine and notify your doctor immediately if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding women: It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while on this medicine. Patients with liver or kidney disease: Use with extra caution. Your doctor may adjust your dose or monitor you more closely with blood tests.
